spec_match.rationale: Runs the explainer's exact call — client.postMessage(msg, {delegate:'popup'}) outside a notificationclick — through a real registered service worker, using the explainer's own scenario 2 (NotAllowedError) vs ignored-unknown-member dichotomy as the detection.

interactive.rationale: Probe button round-trips through the worker and prints its verbatim report; the contrast button runs two real window.postMessage delegate calls.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises the behavioural probe plus the framework contrast; both are on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles missing serviceWorker, failed registration, no active worker, an unexpected error name (printed verbatim, flagged for upstream), and the delivered-message confirmation that distinguishes ignored-option from lost-message.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5091965583622144, the explainer's key-execution-scenarios section and the capability-delegation spec.

conformance.rationale: Is the named observation route for the suite's delegate-outside-notificationclick manual assertion; its contrast call is the same contract as the capability-delegation-framework-validates throws assertion (which passes on Chromium 141).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (Playwright CDP): worker registered and active at the feature scope; probe ran the real call — no exception, probe-delivery message arrived — and the page concluded NOT implemented, exactly the honest branch; contrast threw a real NotSupportedError for the unknown capability (framework live) and reported payment's observed no-throw verbatim; zero page errors, 0px overflow both classes; screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts registration, the supported branch (NotAllowedError), the unsupported branch tied to actual delivery, the unexpected-error branch as a failure, and the framework contrast.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; verdict colours use emerald-dark/rose; buttons pair background and color.

accessibility.rationale: Verdicts and outputs are aria-live polite, buttons labelled by visible text, code samples focusable, visible focus outlines.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Driven at both classes: 0px overflow, single-column stages, 44px buttons.

openQuestions.title: Observe the NotAllowedError branch on a flagged build
openQuestions.detail: With --enable-experimental-web-platform-features on a build carrying CapabilityDelegationPopup, the probe should flip to the supported verdict (NotAllowedError, no delivery). Capture that run and record whether the error message names the missing notificationclick context.

openQuestions.title: Window-side payment delegation did not throw without activation — track the spec/implementation gap
openQuestions.detail: The capability-delegation spec describes initiation as activation-consuming, which reads as NotAllowedError without activation; observed Chromium 141 accepts delegate:'payment' silently when no activation is present. The page reports the raw outcome without inferring. Worth checking the current spec text/Chromium behaviour and tightening the copy if either moves.

guidanceConsulted.query: feature detection unknown dictionary member ignored
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Detection must come from an observable behavioural difference, never from the absence of an exception alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The probe's two worlds produce opposite events (exception vs delivered message); delivery is positively confirmed before the unsupported verdict.

guidanceConsulted.query: status updates live region aria-live announce result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce asynchronous verdicts via polite live regions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Registration state, probe verdict and contrast output are aria-live polite.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: overflow-wrap:anywhere on verdicts and outputs; 0px overflow measured at 360px.

summary: A sound behavioural feature-detect for a surface with no window-side property: the worker runs the explainer's forbidden-context call and the page separates exception, delivery, and unexpected-error outcomes verbatim. On Chromium 141 the honest unsupported branch ran end to end, and the framework contrast proved the underlying Capability Delegation machinery live via a real NotSupportedError.
